narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This means the bank sees a clear majority chance that you would struggle to repay the loan, so your application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and your credit history. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while most (59%) have no checking account at all. This strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

The duration of credit you asked for also worked heavily against you. At 42 months, your request is more than twice as long as the average 19 months seen among people who were approved. Longer loan terms increase perceived risk, so this was the second strongest factor driving the denial.

Your credit history of having critical or other existing credits actually provided some positive influence and slightly pulled the prediction back toward approval. However, this helpful effect was not strong enough to overcome the negative impact of your account status and the very long repayment period.

To improve your chances next time, bring your checking account back into positive territory, consider requesting a shorter loan term that better matches what successful applicants typically ask for, and continue managing your existing credit responsibly. These changes would likely make a significant difference in future applications.
